title: Implement runtime hardware-profile loader + override precedence (env/config/fleet defaults)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
We need a production-safe mechanism for selecting and applying a versioned hardware tuning profile at runtime (H100/B200/L40S) with a deterministic override order.

This ticket covers:
- Runtime-side loader that resolves (a) hardware detection, (b) profile pack source, (c) precedence order across fleet defaults, deployment configs, and env overrides.
- Compatibility and fallback behavior (unknown GPU strings, MIG/partitioning, missing pack, incompatible pack version).
- Backward compatibility plan so existing runtime config continues to work and profiles can be introduced gradually.
- Rollout/rollback primitives so oncall can disable profiles per pool/region quickly.

Non-goals:
- Defining the profile schema keys themselves (ENG-4822)
- Hardware-specific tuning content (H100/B200/L40S preset tickets)

References:
- Confluence: profile schema + compatibility rules (sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/profile-schema-and-compatibility-rules.json)
- ADR: distribution and override order (sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-hardware-tuning-profiles-distribution-and-override-order.json)
body:
## Background
We’re introducing a “hardware tuning profiles pack” that defines curated runtime config presets per GPU SKU. For this to be safe-by-default and support Hosted/Dedicated/Private, the runtime must:
1) reliably detect the GPU SKU (including provider string variants),
2) select a profile deterministically,
3) apply overrides in a clear precedence order,
4) expose enough telemetry/debug info for oncall to quickly identify what config is actually in effect.

This ticket is specifically about the loader + override semantics, not the tuning values.

## Goals
- Deterministic and documented precedence across:
  - fleet defaults (pool/region level)
  - deployment-level config (Helm / runtime config file)
  - route/model-level overrides (where supported)
  - env vars (for emergency toggles)
- Safe fallbacks when:
  - GPU SKU is unknown/ambiguous
  - profile pack is missing
  - profile pack version is incompatible with runtime
  - MIG/multi-GPU nodes are detected
- Backward compatible with existing configs:
  - No behavior change unless profile selection is explicitly enabled (or fleet default turns it on)
  - Existing runtime config keys remain supported; profiles act as defaults that can be overridden
- Operational readiness:
  - A single toggle to disable profile selection and return to “legacy defaults”
  - Log + metric visibility into selected profile and override sources

## Proposed override order (high-level)
From lowest precedence to highest precedence (later wins):
1) Runtime compiled defaults (legacy)
2) Selected hardware profile defaults (from profile pack)
3) Fleet defaults (pool/region config: hosted + dedicated)
4) Deployment config file / Helm values (dedicated + private)
5) Per-route / per-model overrides (where runtime supports it; initially a narrow subset)
6) Environment variables (emergency / canary overrides)

Notes:
- Env vars are intentionally “sharp tools” and should be limited to a small set of keys + a global disable.
- The override order must be identical across Hosted, Dedicated, Private (even if some layers are absent in a given mode).

## Detailed design
### 1) Inputs / config sources
- Hardware detection:
  - Read primary GPU identifiers via NVML where available (PCI device ID + product name).
  - Normalize provider SKU strings for known variants (see Slack thread: fleet-detection gpu sku variants).
  - Explicit handling for MIG: treat as “partitioned H100/L40S/etc” and either map to a safe profile variant or fall back to legacy defaults depending on guardrails.
- Profile pack location:
  - Support “baked-in pack” shipped with runtime as the default.
  - Optional external pack path for Private deployments (file path mounted via Helm/sidecar) with explicit version pin.
- Deployment config:
  - Existing runtime config file continues to load (YAML/JSON depending on deployment mode).
  - Helm values should translate into the same internal config structure.
- Env vars:
  - `RW_RUNTIME_PROFILE_ENABLE=0/1` (global)
  - `RW_RUNTIME_PROFILE_ID=<explicit profile id>` (force selection; guarded)
  - `RW_RUNTIME_PROFILE_PACK_PATH=<path>` (private-only / allowlist)
  - `RW_RUNTIME_PROFILE_DEBUG_DUMP=1` (prints effective config; rate-limited)

### 2) Loader algorithm (pseudocode)
1. Load legacy runtime defaults.
2. Detect hardware and resolve `gpu_sku_normalized`.
3. Determine whether profile selection is enabled:
   - Env var override (highest)
   - Else deployment config
   - Else fleet default
   - Else disabled (legacy behavior)
4. Resolve profile pack (baked-in by default; external path only if configured and validated).
5. Select profile:
   - If `RW_RUNTIME_PROFILE_ID` set, attempt to load that profile (validate compatibility + guardrails).
   - Else select by `gpu_sku_normalized` + optional mode hint (balanced vs throughput-first) + guardrails.
   - If selection fails, fall back to legacy defaults and emit a structured warning.
6. Merge layers in precedence order to produce `effective_config`.
7. Emit telemetry:
   - startup log includes runtime version, profile pack version, selected profile id, and compatibility status.
   - metrics labels include `profile_id`, `profile_source` (auto/forced), `override_sources_present`.

### 3) Guardrails and fallback behavior
- Unknown GPU SKU:
  - Do NOT guess. Use legacy defaults unless fleet explicitly maps unknown -> safe baseline profile.
- Incompatible pack version:
  - Fall back to legacy defaults + emit error log; do not crash by default.
  - Optional “strict mode” (private) can fail fast if desired.
- MIG:
  - If MIG detected and we do not have a validated MIG profile variant, default to legacy.
  - Emit metric `runtime.profile.mig_detected=1` to quantify impact.
- Multi-GPU nodes:
  - Apply profile per-process based on primary device used by runtime; log all detected devices.

### 4) Backward compatibility and migration plan
- Phase 0 (this ticket): loader is present but selection is disabled by default.
- Phase 1: enable in canary pools with explicit fleet default; keep env var disable always available.
- Phase 2: expand to additional regions/pools after perf canary gates stabilize.
- Phase 3: Private customers can opt-in by pinning pack version + enabling selection.

Compatibility commitments:
- Runtime should accept existing config keys even if profiles also set them.
- If both a profile and an explicit config value are present for the same key, the explicit config value wins.
- Profiles must not be required to start the runtime.

### 5) Testing
- Unit tests:
  - precedence order correctness (table-driven)
  - explicit profile id selection
  - unknown sku fallback
  - incompatible pack fallback
- Integration tests:
  - “effective config” snapshot tests for a few representative combinations
  - env var disable path
- CI:
  - Add a minimal profile pack fixture for deterministic tests.

### 6) Rollout & rollback
- Rollout:
  - Ship in runtime-1.18 with selection disabled.
  - Enable per pool via fleet config in perf-canary pools first.
  - Expand by region after 48–72h with no SLO regression.
- Rollback:
  - Immediate: set `RW_RUNTIME_PROFILE_ENABLE=0` at the pool level (or flip fleet default).
  - Secondary: pin pack version back one (private/dedicated) if issue is pack-specific.
  - Ensure runtime logs clearly show “profiles disabled” vs “selection failed”.

## Acceptance criteria
- Deterministic override order implemented and documented in-code.
- Runtime starts and serves successfully with profiles enabled/disabled.
- Safe fallback to legacy defaults on unknown GPU or pack incompatibility.
- Metrics + logs expose: selected profile id, pack version, and override source.
- Integration tests cover precedence order and fallback.
- SRE sign-off on the rollback primitive (pool-level disable) and log/metric visibility.

## Links (implementation)
- GitHub: PR (expected) runtime load hardware profile based on GPU SKU: sources/github/redwood/pr-21991-runtime-load-hardware-profile-based-on-gpu-sku.json
- GitHub: PR (expected) integration tests for override precedence: sources/github/redwood/pr-22047-add-integration-tests-profile-override-precedence.json
- GitHub: PR (expected) normalize defaults to reduce drift: sources/github/redwood/pr-22052-reduce-config-churn-by-normalizing-profile-defaults.json
- GitHub: PR (expected) CLI to dump effective runtime config: sources/github/redwood/pr-22066-add-cli-tool-to-dump-effective-runtime-config.json

## Open questions
- Do we need a first-class “profile mode” dimension (balanced vs throughput-first) in this loader, or keep that as separate profile ids for now?
- MIG policy: do we map MIG partitions to the same profile with adjusted KV cache budgets, or always disable until validated?
- Should Hosted have the ability to do per-route overrides initially, or defer until after initial pack rollout?

## Reviewers
- Runtime architecture: Noah Patel
- Config schema/guardrails: Ethan Park
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (Neha Kapoor org)
- Infra rollout: Irene Choi / Vanessa Ortiz
comments: 2025-11-19 (Talia Benson): Marking P0. SRE wants a single “kill switch” that’s pool-scoped and fast to deploy. Please ensure env var path is supported in Hosted + Dedicated.

2025-11-20 (Benji Okafor): Drafted override order based on ADR; I’m leaning toward: legacy defaults < profile defaults < fleet defaults < deployment config < env. Concern: per-route overrides complicate precedence. Proposed to keep per-route overrides as a separate layer but only enable for a limited key allowlist.

2025-11-22 (Ethan Park): Please ensure we validate external pack paths in Private. We should not accept arbitrary file paths without an allowlist (container mount + explicit config). Also: compatibility checks must be non-fatal by default (fallback to legacy), with optional strict mode for regulated Private installs.

2025-11-25 (Sean Gallagher): Rollback requirement: oncall must be able to disable profiles without redeploying the runtime image. Fleet default flip is fine for Hosted/Dedicated, but Private needs a documented Helm value + env var approach. Also request metrics: `runtime_profile_selected{profile_id,source}` and `runtime_profile_fallback_total{reason}`.

2025-11-27 (Benji Okafor): Implemented initial loader + SKU normalization; handling unknown strings by falling back to legacy. MIG detection: currently treated as unknown unless we explicitly map known MIG ids. Waiting on Infra confirmation of MIG presence in any pools we plan to enable first.

2025-12-02 (Benji Okafor): PR up for review: sources/github/redwood/pr-21991-runtime-load-hardware-profile-based-on-gpu-sku.json. Includes env var disable, explicit profile id, and structured startup log line with runtime/profile versions.

2025-12-04 (Noah Patel): Reviewed PR. Main request: make merge semantics explicit (later layers override earlier) and log override source at startup. Also ensure we don’t crash on JSON validation failure—log error + fall back to legacy unless strict mode set.

2025-12-06 (Aisha Bello): Please add metric labels carefully—avoid high-cardinality. `profile_id` is acceptable if bounded; do not include raw SKU strings from providers as labels. Also add a debug endpoint/CLI separately; for now logs are OK.

2025-12-08 (Benji Okafor): Added integration tests for precedence and fallback; follow-up PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-22047-add-integration-tests-profile-override-precedence.json. Also added `runtime_profile_fallback_total{reason}` with bounded reasons (unknown_sku, pack_missing, incompatible_version, validation_error).

2025-12-10 (Sean Gallagher): SRE sign-off contingent on having a documented pool-level disable mechanism and clear log line: `profiles_enabled=false reason=...`. Please ensure this is included in runtime startup logs. Also: confirm private Helm value mapping will be documented in Dedicated/Private charts.

2025-12-12 (Talia Benson): Marking Done. Loader merged + precedence tests landed; rollout plan is to ship in runtime-1.18 with profiles disabled by default and enable per pool via fleet config after perf-canary gates are green. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-4828 (gates) and ENG-4830 (release checklist).
